tool_arguments.query: Super Micro Computer AI server revenue Q3 FY2025 quarter ending December 2025

events.content: Super Micro Computer AI server revenue Q3 FY2025 quarter ending December 2025

There is a period mismatch: Super Micro Computer’s quarter ended December 31, 2025 was **Q2 fiscal 2026**, not Q3 fiscal 2025. [[1]] 

For that December 2025 quarter, Supermicro reported **$12.7 billion of total net sales** ($12.682 billion precisely), versus $5.0 billion in Q1 FY2026 and $5.7 billion in Q2 FY2025. [[2]] 

The company described demand for its AI-server and storage technology as a key driver, but its reported financial statements disclose consolidated net sales rather than a separate quantified “AI server revenue” line item. [[2]] 

For reference, Supermicro’s actual **Q3 fiscal 2025** ended **March 31, 2025**, rather than December 2025. [[3]]

tool_arguments.query: Super Micro Computer Q1 FY2026 AI server revenue percentage March 2025 quarter

events.content: Super Micro Computer Q1 FY2026 AI server revenue percentage March 2025 quarter

Super Micro Computer did **not disclose a separate “AI server revenue” figure** for Q1 FY2026 (three months ended September 30, 2025) in its reported quarterly-results release; the reported consolidated net-sales figure was **$5.018 billion**. [[1]] 

Accordingly, **$5.018 billion is total company revenue, not AI-server revenue**, and it should not be presented as an AI-server-only figure. [[1]] 

Management characterized the quarter as supported by its AI portfolio and disclosed more than **$13 billion of Blackwell Ultra orders**, but that order-book disclosure is also not recognized Q1 AI-server revenue. [[1]]

Related coverage:
**Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: SMCI): volatility, S&P 500 inclusion, and short-seller risk.** [[1]]

- **Volatility remains unusually high:** SMCI traded between $20.53 and $55.04 from October 17, 2025 through October 16, 2026—a 168.1% low-to-high spread—and fell 9.86% in the October 16, 2026 session alone, closing at $31.63. [[1]]
- **The latest options indicators also imply exceptional risk:** reported historical volatility was 99.53%, implied volatility was 70.35%, and the five-day options-implied move was 6.44%. [[2]]
- **S&P 500 inclusion was a major catalyst:** S&P Dow Jones Indices announced on March 1, 2024 that SMCI would move from the S&P MidCap 400 into the S&P 500 effective March 18, 2024, replacing Whirlpool. [[3]]
- The inclusion followed a sharp AI-server-driven rerating; SMCI’s market capitalization exceeded $70 billion and its shares reached a then-record $118.81 in March 2024. [[4]]
- **Index inclusion did not eliminate company-specific risk:** Nasdaq subsequently removed SMCI from the Nasdaq-100 in December 2024 amid delayed financial reporting and delisting concerns, illustrating that benchmark membership is not a substitute for financial-reporting credibility.
